fact_text:
A Venezuelan national is visa-required for Ireland and must obtain a long-stay 'D' employment visa BEFORE travelling to take up employment for more than 90 days. Venezuela is not on the visa-exempt list (UK, Switzerland, EEA).

Commonly believed: Nationals of the UK, Switzerland and the EEA do not need a visa for Ireland.

Actually: Venezuela is a visa-required nationality, so a long-stay 'D' visa must be granted before travel even though the person already lives in the EU (Spain).

Action required: Apply for the Irish long-stay 'D' employment visa before booking travel; do not travel on the employment permit alone.

fact_text: The correct entry route for employment lasting more than 3 months is the long-stay 'D' visa (as opposed to a short-stay 'C' visa).

evidence_quote: If you want to come to Ireland for more than 3 months, for example to study, for work or to settle permanently in Ireland with family members who live in Ireland, then you can apply for a long stay 'D' visa.

fact_text:
The 'D' employment visa can only be applied for AFTER the employment permit has been granted, up to 3 months before the travel date; a decision takes approximately 8 weeks. Sequence: permit granted -> visa applied for -> visa granted -> travel.

Commonly believed: You apply for an employment visa once you hold an employment permit.

Actually: The permit (DETE) and the visa (ISD) are two separate authorisations from two authorities in sequence; the ~8-week visa wait sits on top of the permit wait and defines the real pre-arrival runway.

Action required: Front-load the permit application so the visa can be lodged up to 3 months before the intended start date.
entity_title: Ireland — entry visa after permit timing
evidence_quote: Once you have received a permit, you are eligible to apply for an Employment Visa.

fact_text: The visa application is made from the applicant's home country or country of legal residence — for a Venezuelan legally resident in Spain, that is the Irish visa facility handling applications from Spain, not Venezuela.
entity_title: Ireland — entry visa apply from country of residence
evidence_quote: You must apply from your home country or where you are a legal resident.

fact_text:
A Spanish residence card / TIE (including EU long-term resident status held in Spain) does NOT grant the right to enter or work in Ireland. Ireland is outside the Schengen area, so residence in another EU state confers no visa-free entry for a visa-required national.

Commonly believed: Residence in one EU state does not, by itself, give entry rights to Ireland.

Actually: Ireland is not in Schengen and is not bound by the EU Long-Term Residents Directive 2003/109/EC; a Venezuelan holding a Spanish TIE still needs an Irish 'D' visa. This is the single most expensive misconception for movers who have 'already lived in the EU for years'.

Action required: Treat the move as a full third-country entry: permit -> Irish 'D' visa -> IRP registration, regardless of Spanish residence.

fact_text:
A Critical Skills Employment Permit allows IMMEDIATE family reunification — the spouse/de-facto partner and dependent children can apply to come to Ireland with no waiting period. (A General Employment Permit imposes a 12-month wait.)

Commonly believed: Employment permit holders may sponsor family reunification.

Actually: The Critical Skills permit's immediate reunification (vs the General permit's 12-month wait) is a decisive advantage for a family-of-4 move and should shape which permit is pursued.

Action required: Confirm the role qualifies for CSEP (Critical Skills Occupations List) so the family can travel together.

fact_text:
The spouse or partner of a Critical Skills Employment Permit holder is registered on a Stamp 1G on arrival, which gives the right to work in Ireland WITHOUT a separate employment permit.

Commonly believed: Family members of permit holders may seek employment.

Actually: Stamp 1G means the accompanying spouse can take any job immediately with no employer sponsorship — a genuine dual-income advantage of the Critical Skills route that movers rarely know in advance.

Action required: Register the spouse for their Stamp 1G IRP after arrival; no employment permit is needed for them to work.

applies_to.source_name: Citizens Information — Employment permits and family members

fact_text:
Visa-required family members (a Venezuelan spouse and children) must be granted an Irish 'D' — Join Family visa BEFORE coming to Ireland. They cannot travel on the permit holder's status alone.

Commonly believed: Family members join the permit holder in Ireland.

Actually: Each visa-required dependant needs their own Join Family 'D' visa granted before travel — a separate application track that must be planned alongside the principal's visa.

Action required: Lodge a Join Family 'D' visa for each visa-required dependant; align timing with the principal's move.

evidence_quote: If you require a visa to travel to Ireland you must have been granted an Irish 'D' - Join Family visa before coming to Ireland

fact_text: The Critical Skills Employment Permit needs NO Labour Market Needs Test. Minimum annual remuneration: EUR 40,904 for occupations on the Critical Skills Occupations List (with a relevant degree), EUR 36,848 if the applicant qualified within the prior 12 months, or EUR 68,911 for occupations not on the list. After the permit, the holder can apply directly for a Stamp 4.

evidence_quote: Because the skills are identified as being in short supply, a Labour Market Needs Test is not required.
